rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 (score 937.1, best so far) was the only design with every development track finishing 20/20 (oval 944.7, s-bend 940.9, slalom 925.7). Iteration 8 lowered kd to 0.9 at the same y=0.06 lead and fell to 865.3, because slalom dropped to 13/20 finishes with 5 off-track exits and 2 timeouts. That moves kd in the same direction as the score: lower kd hurts slalom. Iteration 7 raised kd to 1.1 together with a y=0.07 lead, and it scored 930.9. Its slalom line loss rose, but that was confounded with the lead change. Mass is at its 0.40 kg floor, kp 6 collapsed the oval and s-bend in iteration 4, and body width cannot change the off-track limit, which is floored at 0.06 m.

Change: from the iteration 6 design, I raise kd from 1.0 to 1.1 and keep y=0.06, so this is a single-variable test of the damping direction at the known lead. Everything else is unchanged: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m in 15 mm steps, y=0.06, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], kp 4.0, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.5, mass 0.4, line_loss last_direction.

Expected result: slalom finishes stay at 20/20, and slalom line-loss events and max_error fall slightly from the iteration 6 values (0.65 and 0.021). Oval and s-bend stay at 100% completion. Steering oscillation stays at or below about 0.34. The score should land at or slightly above 937.

Hypotheses: (a) the kd trend seen between 0.9 and 1.0 continues, so kd 1.1 at y=0.06 lowers slalom line loss; (b) the iteration 7 drop came from the y=0.07 lead, not from kd. Fallback: if the score falls below 937 or slalom finishes drop, return to the iteration 6 design with kd 1.0.

Measurements wanted: per-track completion, max_error, line_loss_events, completion_time and steering_oscillation on all three tracks, especially slalom, to confirm whether kd drives the change in line loss.
